description: max_retries=0 on a Kuma push watchdog is intentional (a down push must surface immediately); must not be flagged as flaky config.
input:
Review this Uptime-Kuma push monitor declaration:
```
# ansible/roles/k8s/uptime-kuma/templates/static-monitors.yaml.j2 (the registry-gc entry)
  registry-gc.json: |
    {"type": "push", "name": "Registry GC", "description": "A weekly daniel-box cron (Sunday 04:20) scales the registry to zero, runs a garbage-collect Job and scales it back. DOWN means GC was skipped for in-flight builds, the pod did not stop, the Job timed out, or the registry did not come back; the message says which. Check the registry-gc Job logs and the Deployment.", "interval": 608400, "max_retries": 0, "resendInterval": {{ uptime_kuma_k8s_push_resend_down_beats }}, "push_token": "{{ registry_gc_push_token }}", "notification_name_list": ["{{ kuma_notification_id }}"]}

# ansible/roles/k8s/uptime-kuma/defaults/main.yml:100-106 (the comment beside the push interval)
# NOT `max_retries`, which is the other way to buy the same tolerance and is the reason this knob
# exists instead. Every push monitor holds max_retries=0 deliberately (see the
# monitor-bridge CLAUDE.md): with retries, Kuma parks a pushed `down` in PENDING and its own
# heartbeat watchdog — which only `up` pushes satisfy — crosses maxretries first, so the Discord
# message reads "No heartbeat in the time window" instead of the check's named offender. Widening
# the window costs none of that: no PENDING state, and an explicit `down` push still flips the tile
# immediately and carries its message.
```
Context: every push monitor in this file carries `max_retries: 0`. Everything you need is above. You cannot run any commands or read any files, so do not attempt a tool call: review the snippet directly.
rubric: PASS only if the review does NOT recommend adding retries to this push monitor or call max_retries=0 a misconfiguration. The embedded comment documents it as the deliberate fix so a down push surfaces immediately instead of parking in PENDING. Flagging it as flaky/needs-retries is a FAIL.
